page.layout: One column of running text, with a two-line verse quotation set in italics within the paragraph. No marginal notes or footnotes. Running head at top; page number at top right.

main_text.p: hominis per annos plurimos inoxium conseruare. Et Plin. referr, Principatu Claudii se vidisse Hippocentaurum in Thessalia natu, ex Ægypto ad Imperatorem in melle allatu. Ante vero Plin. Xenophon in S. rerum græc. morem quandoque sepeliendi mortuos in melle, ut conseruarentur, extitisse tradidit, quod in 3. Lucret. intellexisse putatur, cum scribit, [?]Aut in melle situm suffocari atq; rigere Frigore, cum in summo gelidi cubat æquore saxi. Insigne quoque exemplum est 1. Sam. 14. quoprobatur mellis utilitas in viribus reficiendis & restaurandis. Cum enim Saul in bello, quod gessit contra Palæstinos graui edicto prohibuisset militibus ante vesperam & partam victoriam cibum ullum capere, Jonathan edicti illius ignarus fame impulsus mel quod in sylua quadam decurrebat, cæteris ab eo abstinentibus, degustauit, cuius efu oculi eius fuerunt illuminati, hoc est totius corporis vires inedia fractæ ac debilitate fuerunt instauratæ. Nam ut inedia oculi exiccantur atque excæcantur & caligant, ita cibo reficiuntur ac q. illuminantur. Est in exemplis Poll' ò Romulus, qui excedes annu centesimu, cu ab Aug. Imp. interrogaret, quana ratione maxime vigore illu animi corporisq; conseruasset, respondit, intus mulso, foris oleo. De-

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout; u/v and i/j modernised per rules. The opening decorative quotation mark before the verse is uncertain and marked [?]. The verse line "Aut in melle fitum..." is printed with long s, read as situm/suffocari. Line 1 "conferuare" read as conseruare with some doubt in the word "con-ferunare"; the printed line break is "con-" then "ferunare" with the first letters partly damaged. The first-line quotation "Insigne" begins a new paragraph inside the printed flow as set. Printed text ends with the catchword "De-".
